parsed.notes: planner_type: _DStar instances persist per goal key in self.planners and are repaired by repair()/process_state() after cost changes (_apply_changes). Switching goals reuses or creates one per key (reinit_on_goal_switch, excluded). Fallback: in _drive, every 37 steps, if cost[p.goal] >= LETHAL_T and a different free goal cell exists, a new _DStar is built from scratch, discarding the old state. This is not a goal switch, so it counts as a fallback. maybe_prune only rebuilds the heap and keeps h/k/b, so it is not a fallback. map: score/occ/seen/cost arrays are written from lidar in _sense and kept on the instance (_recompute_cost). Penalties are cleared on goal flip via _clear_penalties, but the grid itself is never cleared. velocity_selection: _drive follows a carrot chosen by _carrot from the backpointer path (_path). Slow-down and local repulsion are safety layers on top. There is no forward simulation. stuck_handling: _drive's stall branch calls _penalize, which is timeout-style, but it also sets escape_dir/escape_until, which drives a dedicated escape heading. A contact branch sets escape_dir = yaw + pi to back up. explicit_recovery wins by precedence. D*: Stentz 1994 vocabulary (h, k, t NEW/OPEN/CLOSED, b, RAISE/LOWER, L1..L25). ds_open_keyed_on_k: insert() keeps k as the min of old k and new h, and the heap is ordered on (k, y). ds_raise_lower: process_state separates kold < h (RAISE) from h <= kold (LOWER) and propagates each. ds_modify_cost: _apply_changes reinserts CLOSED states (the changed cells and their neighbours) on OPEN, as in MODIFY-COST. ds_stop_rule: repair() stops at kmin >= h[start] or when OPEN is empty, so the rule is present. It can also stop early on max_exp (90000) or the wall-clock budget (10 or 40 ms), hence partial. ds_backpointers: b is set in process_state and followed by _path to drive.
